DocumentName: Tubbs Setback Restoration Project: 2006 Final Report
Description: Tubbs Setback is a 29 ha parcel leased by the U. S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS). It is located along the northern reaches of San Pablo Bay between the Petaluma River and Sonoma Creek, abutting the lower lagoon of Tolay Creek and Tubbs Island to the west, agriculture to the north, and a remnant marsh to the east. Tubbs Setback was diked for reclamation in the early 1900s and farmed until 1983. In 1985, the Refuge initiated restoration work with additional funding from United Heckathorn Trustee Council.  This document reports on the comprehensive biophysical monitoring of Tubbs Setback and highlightd the incorporation of new methods to improve our understanding of early restoration progress. Tubbs Setback has matured over the past four years. The site progressed from a fallow field  (prior to restoration) to a site that remained ponded during low tides (the first year after restoration). The levee bench was quickly colonized by native tidal  marsh vegetation, though non-native plants remained dominant in the upland transition and levee zones. Birds utilized the changing conditions of Tubbs Setback.

DocumentName: 2022 Jordan River/Big Bend Community BioBlitz Project Report
Description: A community science-centered "BioBlitz" was produced by one of the Big Bend Community Science partners, Sageland Collaborative, on August 27, 2022.  There were almost 100 participants at this first event.  The attached report summarizes partners, roles, objectives & outcomes, community participation and results in terms of the number of taxa observed (birds, pollinators, plants and other wildlife).  It also contains sections with community feedback and lessons learned.  Overall the format of the report is highly readable and would be a good template for other reports intended for community outreach

CaseName: Sharon Steel Corp. (Midvale Tailings) NPL Site
DocumentName: 2022 Jordan River Bird Reserve RSRA Training Event & Stream Condition Reports
Description: In 2022, Sageland Collaborative, one of the community science partners involved in the development of the Big Bend Community Science Monitoring initiative conducted a training for "Rapid Stream and Riparian Assessment" (RSRA), their stream and habitat assessment protocol being used on several sites on the Jordan River as well as being widely used in Utah and surrounding states.  The intention of the training was to acquaint other restoration professionals in the Salt Lake valley with the RSRA methodology, as well as conduct an assessment of the hydrologic and habitat conditions of the river.  Site access concerns prevented conducting the RSRA at the Big Bend, so the training was held at the Jordan River Migratory Bird Reserve, another site that had received Sharon Steel Restoration funding in the 2000's.  The assessment was conducted on a reach of Willow Creek, which had been relocated to a channel on the Jordan River floodplain as a restoration action (the water from the creek was intended to support riparian vegetation on the floodplain which has become elevated with respect to the river due to erosion and channel down-cutting).  The report summarizes the RSRA protocol and details the results of the survey on the Jordan River Bird Preserve site
